editorial_intent: Diagram how TREM2 signaling triggers GPNMB-dependent microglial lysosomal expansion and lipid breakdown to prevent neuronal death during organelle decay.
subject: A cross-section of a disease-associated microglial cell showing activated TREM2 receptors on its membrane, driving intracellular lysosomal biogenesis, autolysosome fusion, and enzymatic degradation of lipid debris near an deteriorating neuronal axon.
setting: Framed by a geometric cranial meridian dome, a 24-division circadian astrolabe calibration arc, and a phase-coherent geodesic neural constellation rendered in precise 20% Bauhaus geometric linework.
composition: Asymmetric Post-Constructivist split-plane lithograph layout featuring a left-to-right causal sequence: neuronal organelle collapse on the left flowing into a dense central microglial lysosomal clearance engine, framed by precise geometric arcs.
